stem: A 3-year-old has isolated gross motor delay without other developmental concerns; which referral is most appropriate?
explanation: Paediatric neurologist is the most appropriate referral for isolated gross motor delay in a young child.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a clinical psychologist is not the specific referral for isolated gross motor delay.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because isolated gross motor delay should be referred to a paediatric neurologist.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because an ophthalmologist assesses vision problems, not isolated gross motor delay.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because an ADOS clinic is used for autism assessment, not motor delay referral.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because isolated gross motor delay still warrants referral rather than no referral.
